vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Open a security PR the moment an advisory lands instead of waiting for the weekly schedule. osvVulnerabilityAlerts covers the uv/pip-compile *.lock files that GitHub's native Dependabot does not parse. Security PRs are NOT given a blanket automerge here: only patch-level fixes match the existing automerge packageRule, so minor/major security bumps open as labelled PRs for manual review. This is the continuous-detection half of the pip-audit split (PR audit informational, publish audit blocking — see .github/workflows/ci.yml).

pip-compile.description: The 16 'dependency not found in lock file' warnings, all against requirements-build.lock, are EXPECTED. Do not restructure the locks — or revert the lock-header style — to silence them. They date from #333 (2026-06-09), which rewrote the uv headers to the parseable long form (--extra=X, --output-file=Y): before that Renovate threw a header-parse error and this manager tracked nothing at all, so the warnings are the visible cost of pip-compile coverage actually working. #472 (2026-08-07) took the count 15 -> 16 by adding mkdocs-material. They surface on the Dependency Dashboard as a single deduped 'Repository Problems' bullet (workers/repository/common.ts keys the set on level+message, so all 16 collapse into one), and only on runs where extraction is not served from the repo cache (cache key = base-branch SHA + config hash + manager fingerprints) — so the section appears and disappears between runs rather than being permanent. Cause: Renovate parses --extra out of each lock header into compileArgs.extra (manager/pip-compile/common.ts) but the dep-matching loop (manager/pip-compile/extract.ts) never consults it — it compares every pep621 dep in pyproject.toml against one lock and warns for each one absent, with no notion that --extra was meant to narrow the set. A guard in that same loop means only the FIRST lock referencing pyproject.toml runs the comparison, and that is alphabetically-first requirements-build.lock, whose --extra=container set is our narrowest (build, plus the PyYAML runtime dep) — so the noise is worst-case by accident of filename ordering. The 16 are: requires-python and hatchling (build-system.requires, which can never appear in a pip lock), the intentional compose-lint[lint] self-reference, and optional-dependency pins that legitimately live in requirements-dev.lock / requirements-docs.lock / requirements.lock (including the corpus/matplotlib group deliberately absent from every lock). Update coverage is NOT affected: verified 2026-08-08 with `npx renovate@latest --platform=local --dry-run=extract` that each warned dep is still extracted with its currentValue and datasource=pypi and no skipReason, so bumps still open normally; only lockedVersion, a display field, goes unset. No upstream issue tracked this as of 2026-08-08; the fix would be for that loop to skip deps whose managerData.depGroup falls outside compileArgs.extra (pep621 already tags them) and to skip the requires-python / build-system.requires depTypes.

poetry.description: pyproject.toml is already covered by pep621 + pip-compile. The poetry manager detects the same [project] deps but is not in the python group rule, so it spawned duplicate ungrouped PRs that bumped pyproject without regenerating the lockfiles (e.g. renovate/ruff-0.x, #329).

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions: SHA-pin every uses: with version comment (CLAUDE.md).

Python runtime + dev deps batched into one PR. pip-compile tracks the uv-generated requirements*.lock files: their .lock extension is matched by no pip-family manager by default, leaving transitive pins (e.g. urllib3) invisible to Renovate and weekly lockFileMaintenance a no-op for these files.
Docker base images: digest-pin per CLAUDE.md.

Production runtime + build-stage base images bypass the weekly schedule. Debian and distroless rebuilds carry CVE patches we cannot apply ourselves (no shell, no apt at runtime), so opening the bump PR same-day shrinks the window between upstream patch and our published image. Still manual-merge — the manifest-list-vs-per-arch digest gotcha (memory/feedback_dockerfile_manifest_list_digest.md) needs human verification.

Demo toolchain: the compose-lint pin in scripts/demo records which release the committed GIF was rendered on, so it moves only as part of a deliberate demo regeneration (docs/RELEASING.md), never via Renovate. pillow/numpy and transitives in the same lock stay managed.

Automerge low-risk routine updates once CI is green. Patch-level Python dep bumps, pinned-digest refreshes for GitHub Actions, and lockFileMaintenance go in without human review. Docker base images stay manual because the OCI manifest-list vs per-arch digest check (see MEMORY.md) is not mechanically verified in CI.
